classification.difficultyReason: Read each labelled vertex and use concavity to select a coefficient of 1 or −1 in the supplied vertex-form formula.

content.prompt: Use the formula in Box 22 to write down the equation of each of the quadratic functions sketched below. In each case, the coefficient of $x^2$ is either $1$ or $-1$.

spec.description: Upward parabola, labelled vertex and y-intercept; arrowed axes and both curve ends, with no grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied graphical givens are visible; the equation is withheld.

answer.worked: The vertex is $(1,2)$ and the parabola is concave up, so $a=1$. Substituting into $y=a(x-h)^2+k$ gives $y=(x-1)^2+2$.

spec.description: Upward parabola, labelled vertex and y-intercept; arrowed axes and both curve ends, with no grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied graphical givens are visible; the equation is withheld.

answer.worked: The vertex is $(-2,-3)$ and the parabola is concave up, so $a=1$. Substituting into $y=a(x-h)^2+k$ gives $y=(x+2)^2-3$.

spec.description: Downward parabola, labelled vertex and y-intercept; arrowed axes and both curve ends, with no grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied graphical givens are visible; the equation is withheld.

answer.worked: The vertex is $(3,4)$ and the parabola is concave down, so $a=-1$. Substituting into $y=a(x-h)^2+k$ gives $y=-(x-3)^2+4$.

spec.description: Downward parabola, labelled vertex and y-intercept; arrowed axes and both curve ends, with no grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied graphical givens are visible; the equation is withheld.

answer.worked: The vertex is $(2,-1)$ and the parabola is concave down, so $a=-1$. Substituting into $y=a(x-h)^2+k$ gives $y=-(x-2)^2-1$.
